summary: This excerpt from Book 11 (part 103) of a fiction novel shows Adam, a successful man, confiding to Rebecca about his mother, who died young for lack of love and care while he was a child. Rebecca responds with sympathy, comparing the mother's youthful face to a flower and offering comfort. Adam then sees Rebecca with fresh eyes, noticing her bright eyes, rosy color, and long braided hair tied with bows, as he says goodbye.
one_line: Adam shares his grief over his mother's early death with Rebecca, who comforts him, and he begins to see her differently.
key_facts: Adam's mother was married a month after she graduated and lived only until Adam was ten.
Adam shows Rebecca a leather case containing a picture of his mother, described as having an innocent, pink-and-white daisy of a face.
Rebecca feels old, experienced, and maternal, and longs to comfort and strengthen the tender young face in the picture.
Adam says 'The flower had to bear all sorts of storms,' describing the bitter weather of the world bending his mother's slender stalk.
Adam says his mother 'died for lack of love and care, nursing and cherishing,' and that he can never forget it.
Adam says that all his success, money and power would have kept his mother alive and happy, and that it is now too late.
Adam describes his mother's look of a yellow-curled girl with sky-blue eyes who tied a white muslin hat under her chin.
Rebecca says her own mother is always sad and busy, but once said of John, 'He makes up for everything.'
Adam calls Rebecca 'a comforting little person' as he rises from his chair.
Adam takes Rebecca's slim brown hands in his and says goodbye.
Adam calls Rebecca 'little Rose-Red-Snow-White' and says she is making way for a new girl.
Adam remarks that burning the midnight oil and doing four years' work in three is supposed to dull the eye and blanch the cheek, yet Rebecca's eyes are bright and her color rosy.
Rebecca's long braids are looped one on the other to make a black letter U behind her head, tied with grand bows.
